questions.q: Where did Yahweh say Jerusalem had its beginning and birth?
questions.a: Yahweh said Jerusalem had its beginning and birth in the land of Canaan.

questions.q: What was done with Jerusalem on the day it was born?
questions.a: Jerusalem was thrown out into the open field on the day it was born.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do for Jerusalem after its birth?
questions.a: Yahweh made Jerusalem grow like a plant in a field after its birth.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do for Jerusalem when it reached the age of maturity?
questions.a: Yahweh spread his robe over Jerusalem, and brought it into covenant with him.

questions.q: Why did Jerusalem’s fame go out among the nations?
questions.a: Jerusalem’s fame went out among the nations because of its beauty.

questions.q: How did Jerusalem act after its fame went out among the nations?
questions.a: Jerusalem acted like a prostitute after its fame went out among the nations.

questions.q: What did Jerusalem do with its sons and daughters born for Yahweh?
questions.a: Jerusalem sacrificed its sons and daughters to the images.

questions.q: What did Jerusalem make in every public place?
questions.a: Jerusalem made a shrine in every public place.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would cut off because of Jerusalem’s prostitution?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would cut off Jerusalem’s food because of its prostitution.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say is the difference between Jerusalem and every prostitute?
questions.a: Yahweh said the difference is that prostitutes are paid for their acts, but Jerusalem pays its lovers and bribes them.

questions.q: Who did Yahweh say he would gather against Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would gather all of Jerusalem’s lovers against her on every side.

questions.q: How will Yahweh’s attitude toward Jerusalem change after it is punished?
questions.a: After Jerusalem is punished, Yahweh will no longer be angry with Jerusalem.

questions.q: Yahweh said that Jerusalem had done more evil than what other two places?
questions.a: Yahweh said that Jerusalem had done more evil than Sodom and Samaria.

questions.q: Who did Sodom refuse to help?
questions.a: Sodom refused to help the poor and needy.

questions.q: What did the people all around Jerusalem think about the city?
questions.a: The people around Jerusalem despised it and made it an object of scorn.

questions.q: Yahweh said he would treat Jerusalem as he would treat anyone who did what?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would treat Jerusalem as he would treat anyone who despised their oath and broke a covenant.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would call to mind and establish?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would call to mind his covenant with Jerusalem and establish an everlasting covenant with it.

questions.q: What will Jerusalem’s reaction be when Yahweh forgives it for all it has done?
questions.a: Jerusalem will be ashamed and will not longer speak because of its shame.

commentary.text: A parable showing the first low estate of the Jewish nation, its prosperity, idolatries, and punishment.

Ezek. 16:1-58 In this chapter God's dealings with the Jewish nation, and their conduct towards him, are described, and their punishment through the surrounding nations, even those they most trusted in. This is done under the parable of an exposed infant rescued from death, educated, espoused, and richly provided for, but afterwards guilty of the most abandoned conduct, and punished for it; yet at last received into favour, and ashamed of her base conduct. We are not to judge of these expressions by modern ideas, but by those of the times and places in which they were used, where many of them would not sound as they do to us. The design was to raise hatred to idolatry, and such a parable was well suited for that purpose.

Ezek. 16:59-63 After a full warning of judgments, mercy is remembered, mercy is reserved. These closing verses are a precious promise, in part fulfilled at the return of the penitent and reformed Jews out of Babylon, but to have fuller accomplishment in gospel times. The Divine mercy should be powerful to melt our hearts into godly sorrow for sin. Nor will God ever leave the sinner to perish, who is humbled for his sins, and comes to trust in His mercy and grace through Jesus Christ; but will keep him by his power, through faith unto salvation.
